# **Chapter 1** **Introduction**  {#chapter-1-introduction}

1. ## **Background/Overview**  {#background/overview}

Briefly introduce your project idea. This section will expand the title quoted for the project by explaining the background to the work you propose

The main reasons for using information from external sources are either to complement the contents of the work with relevant data or to provide a different opinion on the issue stated. In both cases, it means adding credibility to the project, making it look more trustworthy and complete. The author should create an analytical review of the previous scientific works on the topic or explore related development. Reference text should be written in quotes and indented and the references marked in \[square brackets\]. “Reference material”. \[1\]

Use IEEE referencing style available in Microsoft word as shown in Fig. 1\. 

![][image2]

*Figure 1*. Word references tab

2. ## **Problem Statement** {#problem-statement}

Describe the purpose, motivation or relevance of the project. Describes why the problem is important. You must convey why you want to take this project and what you hope to learn from your research/development.\[2\]

3. ## **Aims and Objectives** {#aims-and-objectives}

The goal of the project and the main focused objectives of the project are discussed in this section.

4. ## **Scope of the Project** {#scope-of-the-project}

Scope defines what needs to be achieved and the work that must be done to deliver a project. It includes specific project goals, deliverables, features, functions, tasks, deadlines, and ultimately costs.

# **Chapter 2**  **Related Work** {#chapter-2-related-work}

This chapter sums up the past work conducted on the similar area to specifiy that how your work is different from the existing methods. 

# **Chapter 3** **Methodology** {#chapter-3-methodology}

## **3.1 Proposed Method** {#3.1-proposed-method}

This section provides insight into what methodology you will employ in the development of the envisioned system. It is the systematic, theoretical analysis of the methods applied to your study. It can comprise step-by-step procedures, flowcharts, block diagrams or algorithms of the proposed system.
